We propose to minimize the AC1 upper bound by leveraging structured, non-uniform perturbations that exploit the smoothness and decay properties inherent to autocorrelation minimization. Unlike additive block-wise perturbations, our approach introduces multiplicative rescaling and cyclic interpolation, creating exponential decay patterns that dampen extreme peaks in the convolution. The core insight is that sequences with smoother, flatter autocorrelation profiles achieve lower max values, and leveraging irrational rotations through trigonometric mixing helps explore these regions more effectively. We refer to this as a "structured local search with adaptive smoothing."
